model_annotation: Figure 3(a) displays loss curves for training from scratch, plotting the loss on the y-axis against the number of training steps on the x-axis. The x-axis is labeled "steps" and spans from 0 to approximately 1200, with tick marks at regular intervals of 200, using a linear scale. The y-axis is labeled "loss" and ranges from approximately 2.0 to 3.0, with tick marks at intervals of 0.2, also on a linear scale. The plot contains five distinct lines, each representing a different method: Vanilla (blue solid line), StrmLLM (n=380) (red dashed line), StrmLLM (n=256) (green dash-dotted line), SepLLM (n=64) (cyan solid line), and SepLLM (n=256) (magenta solid line). All lines start at a loss value of approximately 3.0 at step 0 and decrease as training progresses. The Vanilla method shows the steepest initial decline, reaching a loss of about 2.2 by step 1200. StrmLLM (n=380) and StrmLLM (n=256) exhibit similar trends, with losses decreasing to approximately 2.4 and 2.3, respectively, by the end of training. SepLLM (n=64) and SepLLM (n=256) show slower initial declines but converge to lower final losses, approximately 2.1 and 2.0, respectively, at step 1200. The lines are smooth and monotonically decreasing throughout the training steps, with no visible peaks or plateaus.
